title: TE-3 — Public Static Content Detail View Delivery
summary: extend the shared main hosted-view and panel-layout contracts, then deliver a lightweight static Markdown table view in public and Manage readers
content_html:
TE-3 — Public Static Content Detail View Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as TE-3, after TE-2 projects exact table-detail eligibility from canonical authoring intent. Content Detail View Concept And Architecture owns the panel/view integration, exact-target, expanded-layout, toolbar, public-composition, and static-source boundaries implemented by this delivery.

The delivery extends the existing shared main hosted-view model and proves it with ordinary rendered Markdown tables in both public and Manage Docs Viewer. It does not add a modal table application, change Markdown source, or introduce managed table tools.

Complete Outcome

Every Markdown table carrying the projected data-docs-content-detail="table" marker in a public or Manage rendered document has a subtle Open table control. Unmarked tables remain ordinary. Invoking the control requests the registered content-detail main view with the exact current document target and table occurrence.

The existing main panel expands through panel-layout projection, the existing main-view toolbar provides Back to document and the presentation label, and the table view provides natural column sizing, a sticky header row, a sticky first column, and one unified horizontal/vertical viewport. Leaving restores the prior rendered-document and panel context.

TE-3 does not resize columns, copy or export data, or persist view state. Dynamic report lists and Review composition remain unchanged.

Current Seams And Expected Size

The likely owners to trace are the shared view registry, main-view host/context, document-view coordinator, view state, panel layout, app runtime/composition, document controller, shared control definitions/renderers, Docs Viewer CSS, and focused browser-module smoke boundaries.

The current indicative shape is 7–10 touched production files plus one or two focused new modules, approximately 350–600 production JavaScript/CSS lines and 250–450 focused test lines. TE-3.0 must replace this estimate with exact files and separated view-foundation, table-adapter, CSS, public-composition, and test diffs. If the foundation requires a new shell, toolbar host, global registry, route model, or materially exceeds the reviewed shape, stop before implementation.

Rough Delivery Steps

TE-3.0 — Trace And Freeze The Existing Model Extension

  • [ ] Trace main view definitions, request/lifecycle context, document mode coordination, main-view toolbar projection, view state, panel layout, rendered-document mount/replacement, navigation invalidation, and public/Manage import boundaries.
  • [ ] Trace current Markdown table HTML/CSS, document mount ordering, existing dormant table wrapper styles, link behavior, and the boundary before dynamic document extras mount.
  • [ ] Trace the TE-2 projected eligibility marker and implicit TE-6 marker, proving that runtime code never parses comments or infers eligibility from table geometry.
  • [ ] Freeze the content-detail view definition, per-document-mount table registry, opaque adapter target, narrow transient request context, supported table target validation, mount-generation rejection, and return/restoration behavior.
  • [ ] Freeze exact-element versus registration-time-clone ownership, detail-time cloning, document-only control removal, duplicate-ID and ID-reference normalization, semantic/link preservation, and registry disposal.
  • [ ] Freeze the expanded-main layout state, prior index/info state preservation, available width/height, toolbar behavior, document navigation response, and narrow/mobile fallback.
  • [ ] Freeze public promotion through one shared public-safe module, explicit route feature/app-kind ownership, and an import graph that does not pull Manage dependencies into the public reader.
  • [ ] Freeze natural table sizing, the single bounded viewport, sticky header/first-column layering, focus, text selection, link activation, and the absence of resize, clipboard, export, and persistence behavior.
  • [ ] Record exact production/test files, reused seams, and rough diffs for TE-3.1, TE-3.2, and TE-3.3 before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: one static document fixture with unmarked, short marked, wide marked, and long marked tables in public and Manage readers demonstrates exact eligibility, target selection, main-view entry/return, layout restoration, sticky intersections, narrow fallback, stale-mount rejection, and exclusion of a dynamic report table. Stop before implementation.

TE-3.1 — Extend Main View And Panel Layout

  • [ ] Register one public-safe content-detail main hosted view through the existing code registry and explicit public/Manage app composition.
  • [ ] Extend hosted-view requests with the frozen narrow immutable target context and lifecycle cleanup without exposing broad runtime state.
  • [ ] Extend view state and panel layout with the named expanded-main projection, preserving and restoring prior index and info state through one detail session.
  • [ ] Register Back and a presentation label on the existing main-view surface, with live state supplied by the active content-detail owner.
  • [ ] Make document/scope navigation and replaced mounts invalidate the active target through existing route and document lifecycle owners.
  • [ ] Prove search, Recent, source mode, metadata Info, and ordinary rendered-document controls retain their current view/mode behavior in each applicable app kind.

TE-3.2 — Add The Markdown Table Adapter

  • [ ] Query and decorate only tables carrying the exact TE-2 eligibility marker in the accepted rendered-document mount before dynamic extras, using a subtle accessible component control.
  • [ ] Supply the exact table target to content-detail without reselecting from title, header text, URL, displayed row, or another table.
  • [ ] Have the table adapter clone and normalize the accepted semantic table into one bounded two-axis viewport with natural widths, sticky header and first column, correct top-left layering, and ordinary link/text behavior; the generic view must not rebuild table markup or parse Markdown.
  • [ ] Preserve the static presentation contract: no column resizing, Reset, clipboard action, download, or persisted viewer state.
  • [ ] Release transient target, scroll, and event state on Back, navigation, mount replacement, or view disposal.

TE-3.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused hosted-view/panel-layout module smoke, marked/unmarked/implicit eligibility, public/Manage import-boundary checks, document-mount target tests, link behavior checks, lint, generated Docs builds, search build, and git diff --check.
  • [ ] Manually review realistic narrow, wide, long, link-heavy, wrapped-text, empty-cell, punctuation, and dark/light tables in public and Manage readers; exercise mouse, keyboard, horizontal/vertical scroll, sticky intersections, Back, and document navigation.
  • [ ] Prove dynamic report grids, docs_subscope, search, Recent, source mode, and Review remain unchanged and unenhanced.
  • [ ] Update Panel Hosts and Control Surfaces, Toolbar Model, and the concise table presentation owner with shipped behavior and the supported extension rule.

Not In Scope

  • column resizing, Reset, and Copy as CSV, which belong to TE-4;
  • diagram migration, which belongs to TE-5;
  • Review route composition;
  • more than one frozen column, user-selected frozen columns, or persisted widths;
  • sorting, filtering, grouping, row actions, selection, editing, formulas, charts, or virtualization;
  • clipboard or download export;
  • stable table identity or direct URLs to table detail state;
  • raw application/report tables mounted after the rendered document;
  • automatic eligibility based on table width, height, overflow, row count, heading, or viewport; or
  • a second panel, toolbar, modal, route shell, or view-state owner.

The Table Enhancements feature owns sequencing. TE-3 table integration begins only after TE-2 supplies the exact eligibility marker. TE-4 and TE-5 begin only after the shared view target, layout, toolbar, return, public composition, and cleanup contracts work independently with marked tables. TE-5 is sequenced after TE-4 but does not technically depend on it.
